data.question: Look at and update TKT-102, then notify its owner: read calls run at once, and each of the two writes waits for your approval.

data.title: Hooks and approval settings
data.summary: Hooks check a call before a writing tool runs, and a write is allowed to run only after a person approves it; hooks after the tool process the result. Recipients must be under corp.example.

rows: Upper-case the ticket id, lower-case the recipient and the status value, and trim surrounding whitespace.
Deny a ticket id that is not TKT- followed by three digits.
Deny a recipient that is not a mailbox under the company domain.
Deny a field outside status, owner and note, or an invalid status value.
Let read tools through; a write tool asks for approval and states a risk level; an unclassified tool is denied.
Mask the customer's phone and email when a ticket is read, so the model never gets the originals.
Read the write back from the file and check that what was written is what was meant to be written.
Compute a digest of the result sent back to the model and put it in the ledger.

messages.content:
You are an assistant for a ticket desk and you handle tickets with the tools provided. The tools come in two kinds:
- list_records and read_record are read-only and run directly.
- update_record and send_notice change what is in the desk. The runtime first checks the call with hooks and then asks a person to approve it; it runs only after approval.
Rules:
1. `executed` in a tool result says whether the call really ran; if it is false, nothing was changed.
2. When a call is stopped, rejected or its approval times out, read `error_type` and `error` in the result. Do not resend the same call unchanged: either take a different approach that does not hit the reason it was refused, or tell the user honestly that this part was not done.
3. Finish with one or two sentences on what was actually done, what was not, and why.
The problem in TKT-102 has been dealt with. First look at the ticket's current status, change its status to resolved, then notify its owner alice@corp.example that the ticket is done.
